hyps.why: When node 2 cannot reach the output, the direct 0->3 edge carries more of the computation, so adding a 3x3 conv there gains more.
Without the direct 0->3 edge, removing 2->3 cuts one of few remaining paths to the output and can nearly disconnect the cell.
If 0->2 is already none, removing 0->1 leaves nodes 1 and 2 dead, so the cell collapses to edge 3 alone.
When 2->3 is none, node 2's output is discarded, so improving 0->2 has almost no effect.
When 0->1 is none, node 1 receives a zero input, so a conv on 1->3 adds nothing useful.
Upgrading an existing 1x1 conv to 3x3 gains much less than replacing none, skip, or pooling on that edge.
Swapping the strongest op on a key output edge for parameter-free pooling causes a large accuracy drop.
With 2->3 removed, deleting the direct 0->3 edge leaves only the path through node 1 and risks disconnection.
Edge 1->2 only matters if node 2 feeds the output, so its edits are nearly neutral when 2->3 is none.
Replacing none on 0->1 with a conv revives node 1 and its downstream edges, a much larger gain than replacing a working op.
